starshipEstimatedLaunch.summary: SpaceX has not posted an official Flight 14 date. Ship 41 completed single-engine and six-engine static-fire testing on August 19-20, and current launch tracking places the first orbital Starship attempt no earlier than September. The previously discussed upper-stage tower catch has shifted to a later flight.

stories.title: OpenAI pauses frontier training as cyber capability nears a critical threshold
stories.summary: OpenAI says it paused a major reinforcement-learning run and tightened workload isolation, network controls, and continuous monitoring after an internal model showed potentially critical cyber capability. The disclosure is unusually concrete evidence that frontier-model security is becoming a constraint on development speed, not merely a deployment concern.

stories.title: OpenAI cuts GPT-5.6 Sol API pricing for three months
stories.summary: OpenAI reduced standard short-context pricing for GPT-5.6 Sol to $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens, versus $5 and $30 previously. The temporary cut applies to the API and eligible ChatGPT Work and Codex credits, signaling intensifying price competition at the frontier-model tier.

stories.title: GitHub brings shared Copilot agent sessions into Slack
stories.summary: GitHub's Slack integration can now start cloud agent sessions from a message, use permitted repository context, investigate failures, implement and validate changes, and open pull requests. The public preview for Copilot Business and Enterprise moves coding agents into the team's shared conversation instead of keeping them inside an individual developer's editor.

stories.title: Robot makers say world models—not hardware—are now the central bottleneck
stories.summary: ACE Robotics expects an embodied-AI breakthrough by late 2027, while industry leaders caution broad commercial use could still take years. The key constraint is high-quality real-world training data that lets robots generalize across unfamiliar physical environments, shifting attention from athletic demos to useful autonomous work.

stories.title: AI pushes IT-services contracts away from billable hours
stories.summary: Large outsourcing firms are increasingly tying fees to business outcomes as customers demand faster delivery and price reductions of roughly 25% to 30%. The change is an early, measurable example of AI productivity altering software-services economics and weakening headcount as a competitive advantage.

stories.title: NASA's Starling satellites demonstrate GPS-free autonomous navigation
stories.summary: The FALCON experiment used onboard cameras and a catalog of space objects to determine Starling's orbit without GPS or ground navigation. Over three days it also improved orbit estimates for more than 200 tracked objects, a step toward autonomous lunar satellite swarms and better collision avoidance.

stories.title: NASA's Roman telescope clears its flight-readiness review
stories.summary: NASA and SpaceX certified the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope to proceed into final launch preparations, targeting no earlier than 7:26 a.m. EDT on August 30 aboard Falcon Heavy. Roman's wide-field surveys are designed to study dark energy, dark matter, exoplanets, and the universe's evolution.
